hold_text: Lands after #11388, the head of the still-open merge queue. ⚠️ THE REASON CHANGED AND THE OLD ONE IS NOW FALSE — this field previously named #11391, whose queue-hold was the blocker; #11391 MERGED as 9dcfcbca, so that text was rewritten rather than left standing as a true-when-written statement about a condition that no longer holds. What blocks it now: docs/claude/work/MERGE-QUEUE.json carries eleven entries, ten of them released by #11391 landing and none of them merged, and this PR is in none of them. It also touches docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json, a SHARED REGISTER — which is precisely the churn the queue exists to serialize (#11440 measured it: 26 merges in a day, 19 of them touching a shared register). Arming auto-merge would put an eleventh out-of-band register merge in front of ten that queued properly. ⚠️ The vocabulary does not carry a 'queued behind N entries' reason, so depends_on_unmerged_pr names the queue HEAD; that is the ordering being respected, stated plainly rather than dressed as a causal dependency. The manager owns the queue and has been asked to add this PR to it. Re-declare to landing:self once the queue drains and the merge slot is free — the slot record on main currently still names #11440, which has itself merged.
why: Tier-1 by content: one appended row in docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json, the session-end duty CLAUDE.md requires for work shipped but not yet proven on the fleet (MI-199 / PR #11433, merged 2547a6a8). No src/, no config/, no order path, no runtime, no CI machinery.
